[[File:Monoiminanomikoto-jinja ichinotorii.JPG|thumb|200px|right|{{center|First Torii}}]]
Monoiminanomikoto Shrine (物忌奈命神社) is a {{ill|Shinto shrine|en|Shinto shrine|qid=Q845945|lt=Shinto shrine|1=Shinto shrine}} located in {{ill|Kōzushima, Tokyo|en|Kōzushima, Tokyo|qid=Q1346527|lt=Kōzushima Village|1=Kōzushima, Tokyo}}, {{ill|Tokyo|en|Tokyo|qid=Q1490|lt=Tokyo|1=Tokyo}}, Japan. It is a {{ill|Shikinaisha|ja|式内社|1=Shikinaisha|2=ja|3=式内社|1=Shikinaisha|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Shikinaisha|13=User:Immanuelle|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyocho|lt=Shikinaisha}} ({{ill|Myojin-taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myojin-taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Myōjin Taisha|qid=Q9610964}}) and held the Rank of Prefectural Shrine under the {{ill|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|en|Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines|comment=this used to link to modern system but that one is too overlinked|lt=Modern system of Ranked Shinto shrines|1=Modern system of ranked Shinto shrines}}.
The shrine serves as the tutelary shrine of {{ill|Kōzu-shima|en|Kōzu-shima|qid=Q301669|lt=Kōzushima|1=Kōzu-shima}}, situated on a hill in the northern part of the Maehama settlement.<ref name="商工会">"Exploring the Historic Sites and Myths of Kōzushima," Monoiminanomikoto Shrine Section.</ref>
== Deities ==
The enshrined deity is as follows:<ref name="地名"/>
* Monoiminanomikoto (ものいみなのみこと)  
**According to the ''{{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|en|Shoku Nihon Kōki|qid=Q1041301|lt=Shoku Nihongi|1=Shoku Nihon Kōki}}'', Monoiminanomikoto is described as the child of {{ill|Mishima Taisha|en|Mishima Taisha|qid=Q650772|lt=Mishima Shrine|1=Mishima Taisha}}’s deity (Mishima-no-Ōkami) and his consort Awahime.<ref group="注">The deity of Mishima Shrine is interpreted as either Ōyama-tsumi or Kotoshironushi, with both officially enshrined today. In Kōzushima, the deity is often identified as Kotoshironushi.</ref>  
== History ==
The shrine's founding date is unknown.  
The first historical reference is found in the ''{{ill|Shoku Nihon Kōki|en|Shoku Nihon Kōki|qid=Q1041301|lt=Shoku Nihongi|1=Shoku Nihon Kōki}}'' entry for the year 840 (Shōwa 7), which states that the deity Monoiminanomikoto resides on Kōzushima and that shrines (Jingū Shiin) were built for these deities. In 838 (Shōwa 5), Kōzushima experienced a significant volcanic eruption on Tenjōzan, attributed through divination to the wrath of Mishima’s consort Awahime being excluded from court Rank acknowledgment.<ref name="神々">"Japanese Gods," Monoiminanomikoto Shrine Section.</ref>
Following this event, both Awahime and Monoiminanomikoto were elevated to the Rank of Junior Fifth Rank, Lower Grade, in 840. The shrine later appeared in the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki|ja|延喜式神名帳|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|1=Engishiki Jinmyōchō|2=ja|3=延喜式神名帳|4=zh|5=延喜式神名帳|6=simple|7=Engishiki|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|13=User:Immanuelle/Engishiki Jinmyōchō|qq=}}'' in 927 as a {{ill|Myojin-taisha|ja|名神大社|fr|Myōjin Taisha|zh|名神大社|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Myojin-taisha|comment=changed title based on wikidata|1=Myōjin Taisha|qid=Q9610964}}.<ref name="地名"/>  
In modern times, the shrine was recognized as a Prefectural Shrine on September 1, 1878, under the Modern typeing System.<ref name="式内社">''Shikinaisha Research Reports,'' Monoiminanomikoto Shrine Section.</ref>
=== Notable Events ===
In 2000, earthquakes and typhoons caused landslides that destroyed the shrine’s main hall and administrative buildings. The main hall was rebuilt in 2006.<ref>[http://www15.ocn.ne.jp/~ko-jinja/ Monoiminanomikoto Shrine] (Kōzushima Shrines).</ref>
== Rituals ==
=== festival ===
The annual festival is held on August 1 and 2, featuring the ''{{ill|Katsuobushi Ritual of Kōzushima|ja|神津島のかつお釣り行事|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katsuobushi Ritual of Kōzushima|1=Ritual Bonito Fishing|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11590475}}'', a simulated ritual depicting traditional bonito fishing.<ref name="かつお釣り"/>  
=== Nijūgohin Festival ===
Held from the 24th to 25th of the Lunar Calendar, this ritual involves nighttime prayers and processions, marking a sea-based deity welcoming ceremony.<ref name="神々"/>  
== Cultural Heritage ==
=== National Important Intangible Folk Cultural Property ===
* {{ill|Katsuobushi Ritual of Kōzushima|ja|神津島のかつお釣り行事|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Katsuobushi Ritual of Kōzushima|1=Ritual Bonito Fishing|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q11590475}} - Designated on December 21, 1999.<ref name="文化財">{{National Cultural Heritage Database|302|713|Katsuobushi Ritual of Kōzushima}}</ref>
=== Kōzushima Village Designated Cultural Property ===
* Tangible Cultural Property  
** Main Hall and Worship Hall (architecture) - Designated on January
 10, 1970.<ref name="文化財"/>
